ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the circuit shown in the figure, the internal resistance of the ammeter is negligible, the resistance $\mathrm{R}_{1}=2.5\Omega$, $\mathrm{R}_{2}=7.5\Omega$, and the DC resistance of the coil can be ignored. At the moment when switch S is closed, the ammeter reads $\mathrm{I}_{1}=0.2\mathrm{A}$, and when the current in the coil stabilizes, the ammeter reads $\mathrm{I}_{2}=0.4\mathrm{A}$.

1. What is the electromotive force of the battery?
2. What is the internal resistance of the battery?

At the moment when switch S is closed, the ammeter reads $\mathrm{I}_{1}=0.2\mathrm{A}$, and when the current in the coil stabilizes, the ammeter reads $\mathrm{I}_{2}=0.4\mathrm{A}$. 1. What is the electromotive force of the battery? 2. What is the internal resistance of the battery?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a single-loop supply path with switch S and the battery on the lower branch, an ammeter A in series on the upper-left branch, then resistor R1 on the top branch. After R1 there is a junction: resistor R2 is connected vertically down to the lower node, and the coil/inductor L is connected on the right between the same upper and lower nodes. Thus R2 is in parallel with the coil L, and that parallel part is in series with R1, the ammeter, the switch, and the battery. Reasoning: At the instant just after switch S is closed, the current through an inductor cannot change suddenly, so the coil branch behaves like an open circuit. Therefore current must pass through R1 and R2 in series. The external resistance is R1 + R2 = 2.5 Ω + 7.5 Ω = 10 Ω. With ammeter reading I1 = 0.2 A, the battery emf E satisfies E = I1(r + 10) = 0.2(r + 10). After the current in the coil stabilizes, the ideal coil has negligible DC resistance, so it behaves like a short circuit. This short circuit bypasses R2, leaving only R1 as the external resistance. With ammeter reading I2 = 0.4 A, E = I2(r + 2.5) = 0.4(r + 2.5). Solve the two equations: 0.2(r + 10) = 0.4(r + 2.5). Expanding gives 0.2r + 2 = 0.4r + 1, so r = 5 Ω. Then E = 0.2(5 + 10) = 3 V.
